output:
**Subject: Knocknacarra reading club — where we've got to, and something I should have done differently**

Dear Niamh,

Thank you for your email of 30 October. I've read it several times and I understand the thinking behind it — the low numbers back in September, and the insurance on the hall going up. Both are fair reasons, and nobody should pretend otherwise.

I wanted to write to you before Wednesday's review meeting, though, because the position has changed quite a lot since that email, and it would be a pity if the pause were settled on the September figures alone.

The club has been running on Tuesdays, 3.30 to 4.45, in the meeting room upstairs at Knocknacarra library since September 2025, and this term it has come on in a way none of us expected. We had five children most weeks in September, nine by mid-October, and fourteen last Tuesday, 3 November.

A few other things have happened that I think you'd want to know about. Salthill Book Nook, and Declan Moran in particular, have given us 120 books — mostly for the six-to-nine age group, and a good number of them in Gaeilge, which has been a real gift for the children who like to read in Irish. Last week one of the boys, who wouldn't open a book at all back in September, asked if he could take two home. He did, and he came back the following Tuesday asking whether he could take two more.

And two sisters from a Ukrainian family started coming in October. The older one now reads to her little sister in English at the end of every session. That alone has been worth the wet Tuesday trudge up the stairs.

There is one thing I should have done differently, and I would rather tell you about it myself than have you hear it from anyone else. I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers' market, and in the course of the chat I got carried away and told her she was welcome to come along on any Tuesday and take photographs. I knew perfectly well that had to come through you first, and I should have checked before I said it. I was wrong, and I'm sorry.

I do know the policy — no photographs of children without your sign-off and the parental consent forms — and I know that any coverage is only good for this club if it's done properly, which means through you and not around you. So I am offering to ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you have seen the numbers and decided what you want to do. If you do want to go ahead on 24 November, I will gladly get the consent forms in from the families myself and do whatever else needs doing, but I won't take a step without your go-ahead.

All I'm asking is that you might have a look at where attendance has got to before the meeting on 18 November, and that you might reconsider the pause. The insurance costs are real and I'm not pretending otherwise, but the club has only just taken off, and stopping it now would be a shame. If it needs reworking, I'd be glad to help with that.

You've done a great deal for this group already, and the children up there are lucky to have it.

Warm regards,

[Your name]
[Phone number]
